annotate_archive_key: Archive: out of the two zones, still in all mail and search (e)
annotate_is_archived: Archived: out of Conversations and Notifications, still in All mail, its labels and search.
area_downgraded_hint: Mail to unclaimed prefixes, or that failed DMARC. Hidden everywhere else.
area_leaks_hint: Claimed prefixes that got mail from senders they were not given to, or mail pretending to be one of those senders. Set whom a prefix was given to above its mail, or with {#code}yuuka prefix expect{/code}.
area_leanings_hint: Mail by the option a model's latest estimate gave the highest probability. No threshold: 51% and 99% both count. Nothing was hidden or moved because of it.
area_unclaimed_hint: Addresses that got mail without being claimed. Claim one here, or with {#code}yuuka prefix claim{/code}.
auth_enroll_done_link: The passkey is stored. The link is used up; sign in with the new passkey.
auth_enroll_done_session: The passkey is stored. It works from the next sign-in.
auth_enroll_link_once: This link registers one passkey and then expires. Registering does not sign you in.
auth_enroll_needs_link: This page needs a one-time enrollment link. Run {#code}yuuka admin enroll{/code} on the server, or use a recovery code at {#recover}/recover{/recover}.
auth_err_invalid_state: This authenticator already holds a passkey for yuuka.
auth_err_not_allowed: The passkey prompt was cancelled or timed out.
auth_err_security: This page's origin does not match the configured WebUI origin.
auth_err_too_many: Too many attempts. Wait a moment and try again.
auth_login_hint: Use a passkey registered for this mailbox.
auth_login_no_passkey: No passkey yet? Run {#code}yuuka admin enroll{/code} on the server for a one-time link.
auth_recover_bad_code: That code did not work. Check it and try again; each code works once.
auth_recover_hint: A recovery code lets you register one new passkey. It does not sign you in, works once, and the operator is alerted when it is used.
auth_unsupported: This browser does not support passkeys.
bind_buttons_user: pressed by Telegram user {id} count as you
bind_cost_group: This is a group: everyone in it reads your notifications. Only the user above can press its buttons as you.
bind_cost_private: If this is you, this chat gets your notifications and its recall buttons count as yours. If it is not, decline: someone else has the code.
bind_expired: The code expired before it was confirmed; nothing was bound.
bind_how: yuuka gives you a code. Send it to the bot from the chat that should get your notifications; then check here who Telegram says sent it, and confirm.
bind_open_link: Open this link in the Telegram account that should get your notifications:
bind_reported: Telegram says the code was sent by:
bind_revoke_cost: {chat} stops receiving anything from the next event on, security alerts included, and its buttons stop counting.
bind_send_command: Send this to the bot from the chat that should get your notifications:
bind_waiting: Waiting for the bot to receive the code; it expires in {left}.
chain_narrows: This only narrows where its mail goes: no passkey. If the primary is down, the mail waits.
chain_widens: Its mail could go somewhere it could not before: this asks for your passkey first.
channels_add_again_cost: Its earlier chats do not come back; bind them again.
channels_add_cost: Nothing is sent until a chat is bound to it, in My notifications.
channels_hint: Telegram bots that carry notifications and security alerts. Tokens are sealed in the database and never shown again; adding a bot or giving it a new token asks for your passkey.
channels_locked: The server has no key, so no channel runs and no token can be set. Mail still arrives.
channels_on_host: Or on the host, with the token from a file or standard input:

match.nPlural=one: {name}'s token is erased and its {n} bound chat stops receiving anything, security alerts included.
match.nPlural=other: {name}'s token is erased and its {n} bound chats stop receiving anything, security alerts included.

channels_token_cost: The new token must be {bot}'s: its chats stay bound to that bot.
channels_token_hint: From @BotFather. Telegram is asked whose it is.
credentials_issue_legend: Issue a token or an SMTP password
credentials_label_hint: What it is for, e.g. the machine
credentials_on_host: Scripts and automation can issue the same on the host:
credentials_revoke_cost_smtp: {who}'s next SMTP submission with it is refused.
credentials_scopes_hint: Each one ticked, no defaults. Give only what it uses.
credentials_smtp_scope: An SMTP password only submits mail (submission:send). Which addresses it sends as, and how far, the grants decide.
drafter_accepted: Accepted, and the rule is saved. It runs on mail that arrives from now on.
drafter_no_candidates: This message has no sender, list or receiving prefix to draw a condition from.
drafter_not_past: Mail already here is left alone until you apply the rule to it.
drafter_saved: Rule saved. It runs on mail that arrives from now on.
drafter_title: Handle mail like this from now on
drafter_title_accept: Accept, and handle mail like this from now on
drafter_when: Mail like this is mail where
facts_auth_not_received: none: sent by this system, never received
facts_warn_header_only_too_large: the original was too large to fetch from the mailbox, so its body is not here
facts_warn_header_only_unfetchable: the mailbox would not return the body, so it is not here
facts_warn_downgraded_text: treat as suspect; hidden from default lists
facts_warn_forged: the From address is probably forged
facts_warn_leak: {to} was not given to {domain}, which sent this
facts_warn_leak_unproven: {to} was not given to this sender, who is unproven
facts_warn_quarantined_text: the MIME structure could not be parsed cleanly; content may be incomplete
facts_warn_spoof: claims to be {domain}, whom {to} was given to, but DMARC did not prove it
facts_warn_unverified_text: no result from the trusted receiver, so the sender is unproven
grant_cost_allowlist: {who}'s mail as {as} to anyone not on the allowlist stays a draft.
grant_cost_allowlist_remove: {who}'s mail as {as} to the entries taken off stays a draft.
grant_cost_draft: Every submission by {who} as {as} stays a draft until a person confirms it.
grant_cost_hold: Mail the review passes waits {window} for a recall before it is sent.
grant_cost_limit: {who}'s submissions as {as} beyond the new limit stay drafts.
grant_cost_none: {who} may no longer use {as}: SMTP submissions are refused, the rest stay drafts.
grant_cost_review: {who}'s mail as {as} goes through the review checks and waits out a recall window before it is sent.
grant_cost_suspend: Every submission by {who} as {as} stays a draft, and its held mail is recalled instead of sent, until resumed on the host.
grant_cost_thread: {who}'s mail as {as} to anyone outside the thread it answers stays a draft.
grants_defaults_hint: An empty number takes the default of the principal's kind.
grants_none: No grants. Without one, the defaults of each kind of principal apply.
grants_nothing_tighter: Nothing is tighter than this grant short of removing it.
grants_on_host: Or set one on the host:
grants_opt_new: New recipients per day at most
grants_owner_cap_refused: This identity belongs to a person: anyone else is capped at draft.
grants_owner_capped: Capped at drafts: the address belongs to {owner}, and only they send as it. Stored: {stored}.
grants_remove_widens: Afterwards the default applies: {summary}, wider than now in {fields}; it asks for your passkey first.
grants_resume_cost: Afterwards: {summary}. It asks for your passkey first.
grants_suspended_why: Suspended: every submission stays a draft.
grants_tighten_legend: One change at a time, only tighter than now
grants_widening: That lets more through; tightening only tightens. Use Change… (it asks for your passkey), or on the host:
history_archived: Archived, so it is in neither zone. The changes:
history_classifier: In {zone}, as yuuka's classifier put it. The changes:
history_empty: Nobody has labelled, moved or archived it.
history_label: Where its labels, zone and archived state came from
history_moved: In {zone}, moved there by {who}. The changes:
identities_address_hint: *@zone stands for every address of the zone without an identity of its own
identities_disable_cost: Nothing more goes out as {address}: submissions stay drafts, held mail is recalled instead of sent.
identities_human_owner: Owned by {owner}, who sends as it without a grant; anyone else stops at a draft.
identities_no_transport: This process has no outgoing transport (YUUKA_TRANSPORTS), so an identity would have nothing to send with. Configure one on the host first.
identities_on_host: Or add one on the host:
identities_own_owner: Owned by {owner}; without a grant its mail is reviewed, then held for a recall window.
identities_pattern_cost: Every address @{zone} without an identity of its own sends as this one, with its owner and grants.
identities_taken_over: Disabling it would hand the address to {pattern}, its owner and its grants, which may let more through; it asks for your passkey first.
label_case_differs: Labels are case-sensitive; in use already:
label_reserved: Cannot start with $ or a backslash
leak_given_to_nobody: given to nobody yet: {#code}yuuka prefix expect{/code}
leak_none: No claimed prefix got mail it should not have.
locked_banner_body: The server has no key (YUUKA_KEK_FILE). Mail still arrives; transports with a password hold their mail and no notification channel runs until the key is back.
nav_drafts_title: {open} being written, {held} held for a person
nav_leaks_title: claimed prefixes that got mail from senders they were not given to
nav_leanings_title: What a model's estimates lean to; they act on nothing

match.countPlural=one: {count} wants a look: delivery unknown, failed or partly delivered
match.countPlural=other: {count} want a look: delivery unknown, failed or partly delivered

match.countPlural=one: {count} held: goes out when its recall window ends
match.countPlural=other: {count} held: each goes out when its recall window ends

nav_proposals_title: suggested by agents, waiting for your decision
notes_cites_label: Cites: the passages the note relies on
notes_delete_cost: Removes {who}'s note; the mail itself does not change.
notes_delete_cost_own: Removes your note; the mail itself does not change.
notes_needs_cite: A note cites at least one passage.
notes_no_selection: Select text in the mail first.
notes_placeholder: What this mail is about, for you and whoever reads it later. Plain text.
notifications_hint: Telegram chats that get your notifications. Each gets the events ticked; security alerts go to all of them, always.
notifications_locked: The server has no key, so no channel runs: nothing is sent, and no chat can be bound until the key is back.
notifications_no_channel: There is no notification channel to bind a chat on yet.
notifications_on_host: A chat for someone else is bound on the host:
offer_moved_conversations: Moved to Conversations. Do the same for mail like this from now on?
offer_moved_notifications: Moved to Notifications. Do the same for mail like this from now on?
prefix_expect_hint: Domains, separated by commas; empty clears them.
prefix_unclaim_cost: Its mail is downgraded again and leaves the zones; nothing is deleted.
prefix_unclaimed_facts: Not claimed: its mail is downgraded and nothing about it notifies.
problem_secrets_locked: The server has no key for third-party secrets (YUUKA_KEK_FILE), so this cannot be done now.
problem_elevation: That lets more through, which needs your passkey again first.
problem_widening: That lets more through; tightening only tightens.
proposal_conflict: This proposal was decided already, or has expired
proposal_expired: Expired: nobody decided it in time. Nothing was changed.
read_link_mismatch: The text names another site; this link goes to {host}
read_no_anchor: There is no {anchor} in this message; it may have been cited from an older view.
pull_app_password: Gmail wants an app password, not the account's own.
pull_authserv_hint: Whose Authentication-Results this mail trusts; blank trusts none.
pull_banner_paused: Paused by a person {when}: nothing is pulled until it is resumed.
pull_banner_refused: The server refused the password, so pulling {name} is paused. Check the password (Gmail wants an app password) and give it again with Edit. Resume tries the same one again, and repeated wrong passwords can lock the mailbox.
pull_budget_hint: Fetched per day; 0 for no limit.
pull_cost: Mail of {address} comes in from {destination}, and the password goes there only.
pull_default_closed: Others without a setting of their own may not read it.
pull_default_readable: Others without a setting of their own may read it.
pull_hint: Mailboxes yuuka pulls over IMAP, read-only, and who may read each account. Passwords are sealed and never shown again; adding a mailbox, letting more mail in and letting someone read an account ask for your passkey.
pull_locked: The server has no key, so no password can be set and no mailbox is pulled. Mail through the catch-all still arrives.
pull_locked_password: The server has no key: a password cannot be sealed now.
pull_max_size_hint: Larger mail is kept header only.
pull_name_taken: An account {name} exists already, or did: a removed account keeps its name.
pull_not_synced: Not synced yet: a running yuuka serve starts on it.
pull_on_host: Or on the host, with the password from a file or standard input:
pull_other_hint: Mail that reaches the deployment's own domains. Who may read it is set here as for a mailbox.
pull_rematching: the server renumbered it: matching what was pulled
pull_remove_cost: {name} stops being pulled and its password is erased. Its mail stays here, {address} stays claimed, and the name is not used again.
pull_sync_asked: Asked for a round; the running server takes it within seconds.
pull_sync_asked_paused: Asked for a round; it waits until the mailbox is resumed.

match.nPlural=one: Logged in as {user} and can read {n} folder. No mail was fetched.
match.nPlural=other: Logged in as {user} and can read {n} folders. No mail was fetched.

pull_test_refused: The server refused the password. Repeated tries can lock the mailbox; Gmail wants an app password.
pull_tightens: Only narrows what is pulled: no passkey needed.
pull_trusts_none: Trusts no receiver's Authentication-Results, so sender checks on this mail report nothing.
reading_fold_facts: Fold the facts into one line
review_advisory: Worth a look before it goes; these hold nothing back:
review_found_code: a code in the {where}, extracted from
review_found_link: a sign-in link in the {where}, extracted from
review_link_unseen: — {domain} never seen from a verified sender, a recipient or the allowlist
review_recall_conflict: It is no longer held: already released, or already recalled.
review_recall_cost: Nothing is sent; it goes back to Drafts. Two recalls by a person within a day suspend the grant.
review_recall_not_yours: Only a person, or whoever submitted it, can recall it ({scope}).
review_recalled: Recalled: back in Drafts, nothing was sent.
review_ref_unknown: is no message the sender can see
review_resume_on_host: Every submission stays a draft until it is resumed, under Grants in the settings or on the host:
review_suspended: Recalled twice within a day: {who}'s grant on {identity} is suspended.
review_suspended_others: Its other held mail ({n}) was recalled too.
review_unreadable: cannot be read by the checks
rule_apply_disabled: Only an enabled rule that this version understands can be applied
rule_json_invalid: Not a match tree: one of all, any, not, or field/op/value.
rule_json_only: These conditions do not fit the form; edit them as JSON.
rule_preview_failed: {failed} ran out of time and do not match
rule_preview_needs_action: Choose what it does to see how much mail it would change.
rule_preview_overruled: {overruled} keep what a person or an agent decided
rule_priority_hint: Rules run lowest first; the first match sets the zone, archive and notification, labels add up
rule_revert_cost: Every change this rule made to mail is set back, unless someone changed it again since. The rule itself stays.
rule_warn_unverified_from: Anyone can forge From: add “From proven by DMARC is yes”
rules_arrival_only: A rule runs on mail as it arrives. Changing it does not change mail already here; apply or take back does.
rules_delete_cost: It stops running; what it did stays until taken back.
rules_hint: Rules run on mail as it arrives, in order. They only label, move, archive and quiet notifications; nothing a rule does sends mail.
rules_none: No rules yet. “Mail like this…” in the reading pane drafts one from a message.
rules_unsupported_why: This version cannot evaluate the rule, so it matches nothing:
search_help_intro: Press an example to add it. All items must match; put a value with spaces in {#code}"quotes"{/code}.
search_hint: {#code}{term}{/code} was searched as text. Did you mean {#code}{suggest}{/code}?
search_op_after: received at or after: a date, an RFC 3339 time, or -12h, -7d, -2w
search_op_deliveredto: the prefix yuuka delivered it to: whom you gave the address, unlike to:
search_op_not: a leading - leaves out what matches
search_op_text: words and phrases in subject, people or body
search_op_to: To as the sender wrote it, name or address
search_op_triage: what a model's estimate leans to
search_problem_invalid: This query cannot be read as written:
search_problem_scope: This session lacks the scope this condition needs:
search_problem_unsupported: This condition is reserved and not supported yet:
search_value_downgraded: failed DMARC, or to an unclaimed prefix
secret_locked_key_missing: locked: the key it was sealed under is not loaded
secret_locked_no_key: locked: the server has no key (YUUKA_KEK_FILE)
secret_locked_set_again: locked: it does not open as sealed, so the database may have been altered; check where it goes, then set it again
secret_once: Shown this once. Copy it now: once closed it cannot be recovered, only revoked and issued again.
send_body_placeholder: Write in Markdown. > quotes, a blank line starts a paragraph.
send_confirm_detail: it is queued with you as the approver (§8.9)
send_held_no_grant: Held as a draft: no grant
send_held_nothing_sent: Nothing was sent. The draft stays in Drafts; a person can confirm it there.
send_held_nothing_sent_owner: Nothing was sent. The draft stays in Drafts; only {name} can confirm it.
send_no_draft_scope: This session may not write drafts ({scope}).
send_no_grant_theirs: the address is {owner}'s, and you have no grant to send as it
send_no_grant_yours: the address is yours, and you have no grant to send as it
send_no_identities: No identity to send as. Add one under Identities in the settings, or on the host with {#code}yuuka identity add{/code}.
send_no_identity_detail: the draft is kept, but it cannot be sent as it is
send_only_owner_confirms: Held: only {name} can confirm mail as this address
send_only_owner_sends: Held: only {name} can send as this address
send_only_owner_sends_detail: it is {name}'s, and you cannot send as it (§8.9)
send_problem_conflict: Already submitted: the draft has gone to the outbox
send_problem_invalid_body: Something in the draft is not valid
send_problem_no_identity: No identity covers this From address
send_problem_not_found: Not found: it may have been deleted
send_problem_rate_limited: Too many requests; try again in a moment
send_problem_scope_required: This session is not allowed to do that
send_problem_unauthenticated: The session has ended; sign in again
send_problem_unavailable: yuuka is busy; try again in a moment
send_reply_to_unverified: Not replying to the Reply-To {list}: it is not verified.
send_reply_to_unverified_hint: Forged mail uses it to catch replies. Add it by hand only if you trust it.
send_resolve_abandon_risk: Records it as not sent. Nothing more is sent; if the first attempt did arrive, it stays arrived.
send_resolve_resend_risk: Queues it again for the unknown recipients. If the first attempt did arrive, they get the message twice.
send_resolve_sent_risk: Records the unknown recipients as having received it. Choose this when you know it arrived: a reply, or the exit's own log.
send_smtp_note: Submitted over SMTP: the message is kept as the client sent it and is not edited here. Send it as it is, or delete it.
send_tier_review_now: review — sent right after the checks
send_unknown_body: The exit was handed the whole message, then the answer was lost. It may have been delivered or not; yuuka cannot tell, so it does not retry on its own.
send_unknown_only_person: Only a person signed in with {scope} can decide this.
shell_keys: {#k}j{/k} {#k}k{/k} move · {#k}/{/k} search · {#k}r{/k} reply · {#k}c{/k} compose · {#k}e{/k} archive · {#k}l{/k} label · {#k}Esc{/k} close
shell_pick_outbox_row: Pick a row to see each recipient and the attempts.
shell_pick_prefix: Pick a prefix to list its mail.
shell_pick_proposal: Pick a proposal to open the mail it is about.
transports_caps_hint: Everything not listed is stripped from every message sent through it.
transports_hint: Where mail goes out. Passwords are sealed in the database and never shown again; adding or changing a transport asks for your passkey.
transports_locked: The server has no key, so no password can be set, and transports that have one hold their mail. Mail still arrives.
transports_locked_password: The server has no key: a password cannot be sealed now.
transports_name_taken: A transport {name} exists already; configure that one.
transports_on_host: Or on the host, with the password from a file or standard input:
transports_password_again: This moves the transport to another host, port or user: give the password again. A password is only ever sent where it was set for.
transports_password_needed: With a user name it authenticates, and needs the password.
transports_placeholder_hint: A name without a destination yet (from YUUKA_TRANSPORTS, or from before transports moved into the database): it cannot send until it is configured.
transports_remove_cost: {name} stops sending and its password is erased; its name stays in the sending history.
transports_remove_cost_used: {name} stops sending and its password is erased. {used} still name it: their mail needs another transport in the chain.
transports_test_ok: Connected: the server answered EHLO. No mail was sent.
transports_test_ok_auth: Connected: the server answered EHLO and accepted the password for {user}. No mail was sent.
triage_abstained_detail: The model declined to answer; no probabilities were kept.
triage_fold: Fold the estimate into one line
triage_in_hosted: hosted: the mail left this deployment
triage_input_hint: The facts yuuka passed along when it scored, as they were then. The mail's text went with them; it is not repeated here.
triage_mark_title: A model's estimate leans to {lean}. Nothing was hidden or moved because of it.
triage_notice: A model's estimate, not yuuka's finding. Nothing was hidden or moved because of it.
triage_question_key: The question's key, as the filter and agents name it
triage_report_hint: How the latest estimates of the configured scorer fall over the mail you can see. They are a model's estimates: nothing was hidden or moved because of them. A count opens that mail.
triage_report_none: No scorer is configured, so no mail is scored. Set YUUKA_TRIAGE_URL and YUUKA_TRIAGE_NAME on the host; this checks the scorer it reaches:
triage_report_open_lean: Open the mail that leans to {lean}
triage_unfold: Every probability, and what the model was given
undo_superseded: {n} changed again since, left as they are
widen_asks_passkey: Asks for your passkey before it runs; then not again for 5 minutes.
x_code_title: Code found by yuuka in the {source} (confidence {confidence})
x_unverified_title: No DMARC pass from the trusted receiver: the sender is unproven
